fn.en: Describe what is happening right now, and what people are wearing.

items.q: A jacket and trousers in the same colour, for a meeting:
You put this round your neck when it’s cold:
These keep your hands warm:
Soft shoes for sport or for walking a lot:
This holds your trousers up:
You do this in the changing room before you buy:

items.s: It’s cold — ___ your coat before you go out. ⬆️
It’s hot in here. You can ___ your jacket. ⬇️
Can I ___ this shirt, please? The changing room is over there. 🪞
She’s ___ a black dress and red boots today. 👗
I’m going to ___ the photo this evening. 📤
The photo is nice, but the ___ under it is very funny. ✍️

sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which two parts does the verb have when you talk about right now?

items.q: Paul ___ a suit today.
items.why: Right now = am / is / are + verb-ing. Both parts are needed.

items.q: Anita and Paul ___ a meeting with their boss.
They ___ today — it’s a holiday.
“What ___ you doing?” — “I’m buying clothes.”
The dog ___ round the kitchen.
items.why: run → running: one short vowel + one consonant, so the consonant doubles.

items.q: I ___ a meal for six people.
“Are the kids at home?” — “Yes, ___.”
items.why: A short answer never uses the contraction: Yes, they are.

items.q: She ___ a scarf, because it isn’t cold.

items.from: He wears a suit every day.
items.a: He’s wearing a suit right now

items.from: She is wearing a red dress.
items.a: She isn’t wearing a red dress

items.from: I cook a meal for six people.
items.a: I’m cooking a meal for six people at the moment

items.from: The dog runs around the kitchen.
items.a: The dog is running around the kitchen

acts.title: Four captions
text: @aigul_k — “Monday. I’m sitting on the floor of the changing room and I’m not buying anything. My friend is trying on her ninth dress. Send help.” 🪞
@marat.b — “It’s raining and I’m wearing my brother’s coat, because I left mine at the office. It’s two sizes too big. I’m not posting a photo of the trousers.” 🧥
@dana_official — “We’re having a meeting about the new project. Everybody is wearing a suit except me. I’m in jeans and trainers. Nobody is saying anything, but I know.” 🤵
@bekzat55 — “Saturday, seven in the morning. The kids aren’t sleeping, the dog is running around the kitchen and I’m cooking for eight people. Are you free?” 🍳

items.s: Aigul’s friend is trying on dresses.
Marat is wearing his own coat.

acts.title: Four captions
text: My friend is trying on her ninth dress.
It’s raining and I’m wearing my brother’s coat.

items.q: The two-word verb for putting clothes on in a shop to see if they fit.
The verb for having clothes on your body.
The soft shoes Dana has on.
The long warm thing Marat has on because it’s raining.

tts: Hello? — Where are you? — I’m in a clothes shop. Why?
Because I need your help. What are you doing? — What am I doing? What do people usually do in clothes shops? I’m buying clothes, of course.
Well, are you nearly finished? I’m trying to cook a meal for six people, and the kids are making a lot of noise and the dog’s running around.
Why are the kids there? They go to tennis practice on Thursdays. — Not today, because it’s raining.

items.q: Where is she?
What is she doing?
What is he doing?
What is the dog doing?
Where do the kids usually go on Thursdays?
Why are they at home today?

items.sit: A friend calls and asks what you are doing. You are cooking.
o: I am cook at the moment.

items.sit: You describe your colleague in the meeting. He has a suit on.
Someone thinks you are working today. You aren’t.
You call a friend and want to know what is happening there.
Someone asks: “Are the kids at home?” They are.
You are in the changing room with a shirt.

lines.s: I’m in a shop. I’m ___ on a jacket. 🪞
Jeans and trainers. It’s a Saturday!
I don’t know. Two sizes ___ right. 🚫
Not at the ___ — the changing room is dark. 📷

write.q: Write four Instagram captions about right now: where you are, what you are doing, what you are wearing, and one thing that is NOT happening. Use at the moment or right now once.
write.model: I’m sitting in the kitchen and I’m drinking my third coffee. I’m wearing an old jumper and my brother’s scarf, because the heating isn’t working. My sister is cooking, but she isn’t saying what it is. Nobody is looking at their phone at the moment — that never happens in this family.

speak.q: Look around you and say four sentences out loud: what you are doing, what you are wearing, what somebody near you is doing, and one thing that isn’t happening.
speak.model: I’m sitting at my desk and I’m studying English. I’m wearing jeans and a black T-shirt. My colleague is talking on the phone. Nobody is working — everybody is waiting for lunch.
